blocks.heading: Promotion types and their purposes
blocks.text: Advertising communicates a paid promotional message through a medium. Sales promotion provides a usually short-term incentive such as a discount, sample or coupon. Personal selling involves direct interaction to explain an offering and respond to questions. Public relations manages relationships and reputation through appropriate communication and activities. A radio station is an advertising medium, not a separate promotion type equivalent to personal selling. The product is the offering; production is the process of making it. Promotional claims must concern the actual offer and feasible service, not confuse the two.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Nara Tools compares a local advert with direct explanation of a complex tool to business buyers. An advert can build awareness across an audience, while personal selling can handle detailed individual questions. The time and cost per contact may make direct selling unnecessary for a simple low-price everyday item.

blocks.heading: Advertising
blocks.text: Advertising is paid promotional communication through a medium to inform, persuade or remind a target audience. It can reach many people with a consistent message but may reach uninterested people and usually lacks individual clarification. The medium, such as radio or print, is distinct from advertising as a promotion type. Check audience access, budget and message needs.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Hila Bakery places a local notice showing its collection service. The notice can reach relevant readers consistently, but its presence does not prove they buy. Measure response and ensure the offered service is available.

blocks.heading: Sales promotion
blocks.text: Sales promotion uses an incentive to encourage a customer response, often over a limited period. Examples include samples, coupons, discounts or gifts. It can prompt trial but has a cost and may attract people who buy solely for the offer. Distinguish the promotion type from its particular method and from the medium announcing it.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Kena Snacks gives a small tasting sample and advertises the event on a notice. Sampling is the sales-promotion method; the notice communicates it. A larger sample count does not establish profitable paid demand.

blocks.heading: Personal selling
blocks.text: Personal selling involves direct interaction with a prospective buyer to explain an offering, answer questions and seek a sale. It can tailor information and gather feedback, making it useful for complex or high-value products. Staff time and cost per contact can be high, and misleading pressure can harm trust. It is not simply any sale completed in a shop without an explanatory interaction.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Nara Pumps demonstrates its equipment to a business buyer with detailed operating questions. The seller can adapt the explanation and clarify suitability. The same effort may be too costly for a simple very low-value item.

blocks.heading: Public relations
blocks.text: Public relations concerns managing relationships and reputation with relevant publics. Communication about responsible activity, appropriate events or responses to concerns can support trust. It differs from a short-term price incentive and from buying an advertising slot. Credibility depends on conduct as well as messages; publicity is not fully controlled and a promotional event alone cannot erase poor service.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Ota Repairs explains how it is addressing customer complaints and reports the changes honestly. The communication can support reputation if the changes are real. A promise without improved conduct may deepen distrust.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain why fictional Omi Bags’ bag design is a product decision while cutting and stitching are production activities.

Product is what is offered, including features and support. Production is the process creating it. Product is the marketing-mix category; substituting the word production would confuse the offering with how it is made.

blocks.heading: Worked practice: Marketing choices in a coherent mix
blocks.text:
Fictional Omi Snacks sells at N$50 with stated full unit cost N$35. Buyers know the outlet but are uncertain about taste. It compares affordable controlled sampling with a broad awareness campaign and a temporary 10% price reduction. For part (b) only, reliable feedback now shows buyers already know and like the taste but consider the price too high. Other facts remain unchanged.

a Evaluate the promotion options at Omi under the original facts. [12]
b Evaluate the options after the taste and price evidence changes. Explain whether the original recommendation should change. [12]

a Affordable sampling addresses the unknown taste, whereas a broad awareness campaign spends on a need already met. A discount from N$50 to N$45 reduces the surplus above stated unit cost from N$15 to N$10 without proving it solves the barrier. Prefer a controlled tasting trial and measure paid demand, recognising sample cost and capacity. b Taste is now known and liked, so more sampling has less diagnostic value. A price test or revised value proposition becomes more relevant. The 10% offer still leaves N$10 above the stated cost before extra promotion costs, but profit depends on volume and total costs. Test a limited sustainable price response and review paid sales rather than promise a permanent discount. The recommendation changes because the demonstrated barrier changes, not because price cuts are universally effective.
